title: The Apology That Never Came
core_idea: Letting go of waiting for an apology means no longer making our peace depend on someone else's words, and offering ourselves the acknowledgement we needed.
text: Some of us are still waiting for an apology that may never come. We replay the old conversation. We imagine the words they should have said. But that waiting can keep the door to an old room open, and the cold keeps drifting in. Letting go here doesn't mean pretending it didn't matter. It means deciding that your peace no longer depends on someone else's words. You might even say to yourself what you needed to hear: that it wasn't fair, that you deserved care. Sometimes the apology we need most is the acknowledgement we finally give ourselves. And then, slowly, the door can close.
description: A gentle reflection on letting go of an apology that may never come, and giving yourself the acknowledgement you needed.
